title: runtime-role-is-a-second-axis
owner: CC (the census, the code, the proofs). Akien (the axis name, whether TOOLS means this, and the signature gate on any new class or axis definition).
intention: Settle the classification vocabulary: what a thing IS for proving purposes (node_class) and what it ACTS AS at runtime are two different questions jammed into one field. Separate them, or prove the second one is not needed.
why: Akien named a felt gap — TOOLS — and the census says he is right that a category is missing. Across 38 lab charters, 'device' is claimed by 13 and registered by none, with five sub-kinds improvised inside the field: (domain) x2, (instrument) x2, (gate), (stage), plus import_sieve's 'primitive (a library, not a device)' — his tool/device line already drawn by hand. The compound strings are the proof that two axes share one slot: cairn-web_server says 'code-seam (a spine device by role...)' and cairn-harbor_master says 'code-seam (device by role...)'. Two authors independently wrote both axes into the one field they had.
traces_to: Law 1 — the resolver is spent on the novel, not on re-deriving the settled; a vocabulary that forces every author to improvise a string re-derives the same question 13 times. Law 4 — the class is load-bearing physics (/sorted transcribes its gate-set into gates_bound at cast) while the improvised half is policy nothing branches on; the two should not look alike. Law 9 — a registry that no longer knows its own membership cannot answer which lots are still unexcavated.

proves_green.prove_gate: proofs beside the code at cairn/tools/charter/proofs/. Teeth: for all lab charters, node_class resolves to a registered class; the new axis (if one survives) carries every value the improvised parentheticals held; no charter carries a compound string; three uncastable classes (concept-piece, host-seam, operational-driver) either gain workflow_versions or are acknowledged as uncastable. The smallest candidate (register nothing, delete parentheticals, add one field) is tested FIRST — if it wins, the ticket succeeds with less code, not more.
proves_green.entry_gate: BUILDME refuses without a berthed chart chain and intent berth (both on file). Akien's signature gates the axis definition itself.
proves_green.durability: committed and pushed to both repos.

falsifier.proves_red: DONE when, for all 38 lab charters, we can name which node_class it is AND which runtime role it plays without improvising a string. HORIZON: the check must be RUN over the charters, not asserted. WRONG INTENT if the honest outcome is that nothing needs a new category — and the candidate to beat is deliberately the smallest: register nothing, delete the six improvised parentheticals, add one field. If that candidate WINS, this intent fired correctly rather than failed. A node that can only succeed by adding structure is designing for its own conclusion.
falsifier.horizon: The census is already measured (38 lab charters, 13 claiming device, 6 improvised sub-kinds, 12 carrying no class). The build tests the smallest candidate first. Akien's signature gates the axis definition — routes to him and is not settled by the build.

how: Settle the vocabulary: node_class (what it IS for proving) vs runtime role (what it ACTS AS). Name the axis, rule it, delete or promote the parentheticals, handle three classes that cannot be cast, derive or drop membership.
workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(no-improvised-class-strings) -> [PROVED]

watchme.trigger: each poke of cairn/tools/intentions_model_compiler/recompile_gate.sh — the lab is recompiled from the charters at that moment, so the census rides the recompile rather than adding a scan.
watchme.enough: zero unresolvable node_class values across three consecutive pokes AND at least one charter newly authored within that span. Zero-across-a-frozen-corpus is vacuous — the point is that a NEW charter cannot improvise.
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier: charters whose node_class does not resolve, each named, plus the count carrying none. Starts at 13 improvising and 12 absent, out of 38.
watchme.nexus: the node_classes registry — the census and the authority answer from one place.
watchme.consumer: Akien at his signature gate, because this axis is his to ratify.

chart_claim: none, because no chart chain was run — backfilled by ticket inspector 2026-08-26. BUILDME entry gate (buildme_rides_the_sorted) is where this is answered or the chain is run.
cast_by: CC, from Akien's TOOLS idea of 2026-08-11
reshape: node_classes/_charter+why.json says a record defines 'its invariant and its VARIABLE GATE-SET', and 'a pipeline is just the gate-set on a node-class'. Every registered class names a distinct prove_gate: code-seam = the tester runs the proof; concept-piece = a quorum of reviewers; host-seam = measure the HOST plus REBUILD plus an expiring RE-VERIFY; skill = the cairnmap derivation gate; operational-driver = proof plus method-registry plus owned-target. 'device' names NO gate-set — a device is proved by exercising its code, which IS code-seam. So the missing thing is a SECOND AXIS, not a node_class and not a folder. The registry's charter is not violated by this ticket; it is what RULES device out of the class registry.
open_at_cast: Is tool-ness a property of the COMPONENT or of the RELATIONSHIP? import_sieve classed itself 'primitive (a library, not a device)' and is a library to its callers while being a gate at the ruling door. If the kind depends on who holds it, one field per component cannot carry it and a tools/ FOLDER would be actively wrong. This is the assumption the build tests FIRST — it decides the shape of everything after it.

WHERE the field lives (a charter-schema key or a second registry beside node_classes/) and what it is CALLED under build-to-the-tool naming — the term must be derivable from its native-domain use, not memorized.

Is node_class required or optional? Twelve lab charters carry none, eleven of them skills, while 'skill' IS a registered class. Either the field is required and 12 charters are red, or it binds only at cast — different rules, and only one can be true.
members_so_far is stale registry-wide and no door writes it. Law 6 asks who owns that write; the honest candidates are derive-it-from-the-charters or delete the field.

Does Akien's word TOOLS mean this axis? He named a felt gap; the reshape is CC's reading of it. A class or axis DEFINITION is ratified at his signature gate, so this routes to him and is not settled by the build.
charter_deltas_owed: the charter schema — record the distinction: node_class answers 'how is this PROVED', the new axis answers 'what does this ACT AS at runtime'. A compound string like 'code-seam (a spine device by role...)' becomes two fields instead of one overloaded one.
found_while_binding_gates: Of the five registered node classes, only code-seam and skill have workflow_versions registered. concept-piece, host-seam and operational-driver have NONE — so casting any node as one of those three would be REFUSED by the emit chokepoint at its first crossing. Three of five registered classes are uncastable today, and nothing announces it until a voyage dies. THIS TICKET HAD TO CAST ITSELF AS code-seam FOR EXACTLY THAT REASON: it is arguably a concept-piece by content, and that class cannot carry a node. The registry's own gap forced the classification — the incoherence this ticket exists to fix, demonstrating itself at the cast.
siblings: device-ness-is-decided-at-the-shim — defines what the value 'device' MEANS on the new axis. Recorded ruling order: base-device first, then THIS ticket, then alarms.

probe_fired.probe: questions/tool-shaped-or-domain-shaped.json — the corpus's first DISCOVERED probe (2026-07-22), CANDIDATE with ZERO firings until this one.
probe_fired.why_it_was_fired: It is direct prior art for this ticket and it had never run. Explaining an unfired probe's absence is not a diagnostic; calling it is.
probe_fired.it_fired_late: Its charter says it fires at /intent, at the WHAT step. It fired at the cast instead. It would have produced the same split earlier and more cheaply — a point against the operator, not against the probe.
probe_fired.result: It SPLIT the type rather than passing or failing it. The domain concept 'device' is DOMAIN-shaped: imagine BaseDevice gone and Calibre is still a device — a member with zero tool footprint. The current field value 'device' is TOOL-shaped: membership is decided by what inherits BaseDevice, and the measurement says the tool has manufactured SIX members the domain does not have (9 importers vs 3 shims). The improvised sub-kinds are neither — author-shaped, with no tool behavior to imagine away.
probe_fired.it_bit: Before the firing this ticket said 'device is not a class, it is a second axis' and stopped there — which would have carried inheritance-membership forward untouched and re-created the defect one field to the left. The probe separated the CONCEPT from its MEMBERSHIP RULE, which is what makes the sibling ticket device-ness-is-decided-at-the-shim necessary rather than optional.
probe_fired.its_own_tell_confirmed_verbatim: The probe warns that tool-shaped types are 'born from ARTIFACTS THAT ARE ALREADY BEING PRODUCED rather than from a stated need — the members precede the intention.' Thirteen charters wrote 'device' into the node_class field before anyone ruled it a class, and node_classes/ registers it by nobody. The members preceded the intention by 13 — the same accretion signature as `session`, the case that bore the probe.

dependencies: node_classes/_charter+why.json — the registry that defines what a class IS and what gate-set it carries. This ticket reads it and may write it.
intentions_model_compiler — the lab charters are the census corpus; the recompile gate is the watchme trigger.
device-ness-is-decided-at-the-shim (sibling) — defines what device MEANS on the new axis. Ruled order: base-device first, then this ticket.
build-to-the-tool naming (memory) — the axis name must be derivable from native-domain use.
